title: AtomR: Atomic Operator-Empowered Large Language Models for Heterogeneous Knowledge Reasoning

problem.claim: Knowledge-intensive reasoning remains challenging for large language models because of limitations in compositional reasoning and hallucination.

gap.claim: Prior chain-of-thought retrieval-augmented approaches have inadequate reasoning planning and poor incorporation of heterogeneous knowledge.

contributions.claim: AtomR is a framework for accurate heterogeneous knowledge reasoning at the atomic level.

AtomR uses three atomic knowledge operators to retrieve and manipulate knowledge from heterogeneous sources, with reasoning planned as a fine-grained reasoning tree and executed through atomic operators.
BlendQA is a benchmark tailored to heterogeneous knowledge reasoning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three single-source and two multi-source datasets reportedly show that AtomR outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by a large margin.
The authors report absolute F1 score improvements of 9.4% on 2WikiMultihop and 9.5% on BlendQA.
The authors report releasing the code and data.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge-intensive reasoning is difficult for large language models because of compositional reasoning limitations and hallucination.
Existing approaches combine chain-of-thought reasoning plans with iterative retrieval-augmented generation.
Prior work is limited by inadequate planning and poor handling of heterogeneous knowledge.
AtomR introduces atomic operators, fine-grained reasoning-tree planning, and operator-based execution over heterogeneous sources.
The paper introduces BlendQA, reports benchmark improvements, and releases code and data.

source_observation.claim: The framework decomposes complex questions into a reasoning tree whose leaves correspond to atomic knowledge operators.

interpretation.claim: Fine-grained decomposition may make heterogeneous knowledge reasoning more modular and explicit.

application.claim: For systems that reason over multiple knowledge sources, represent planning and execution as composable atomic operations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this operator-based decomposition generalizes beyond the reported datasets or task settings.

source_observation.claim: The authors report improvements on both single-source and multi-source datasets.

interpretation.claim: The reported results suggest that the approach may address heterogeneous-source reasoning rather than only a single retrieval setting.

application.claim: Evaluate reasoning systems separately across single-source and multi-source conditions when heterogeneous knowledge integration is central.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide dataset protocols, baseline details, statistical analysis, or independent verification of the reported gains.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three atomic knowledge operators.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture, training procedure, or data composition.
The abstract does not provide experimental protocols, baseline identities, or result variance.
